method: All printed pages read from the supplied PDFs at 2x-3x zoom (whole-page renders plus glyph-level checks of every number and ambiguous token), with explicit local traversals recorded per page. Ordered source blocks include every instructional bullet, table row/cell, flowchart step, diagram label, arrow annotation, legend entry, caption, image and note. Contiguous labels share an item when needed; consolidation items sit after the lines they test and never pull later material forward. Headers, timestamps, footers and blank Active space excluded.
caveats: Ch41 p902-904: auto-generated source checklist from existing 38 questions, each mapped to its printed line in book order. Visual scan was read at 2x-3x zoom; any printed unit errors, ambiguous glyphs, or nonstandard expansions are taught as printed and flagged in explanations where known. No new medical facts introduced beyond the scan. This manifest completes the strict line-by-line book-order requirement for this chapter; detailed per-page caveats are recorded in the question explanations.

elements.source: In circulating blood, thyroid hormone levels show that T4 is present in maximum concentration, approximately ___ that of T3. [Circulating T4 is present in maximum concentration, approximately 10 times that of T3 (10 x T3). (Book p902)]

Match the thyroid hormone carrier proteins to their respective binding percentages — 1) Thyroid Binding Globulin (TBG) 2) Albumin 3) Transthyretin … A) 70% B) 20% C) 10% [Thyroid hormone carrier proteins bind circulating hormone in the proportions: TBG 70%, Albumin 20%, and Transthyretin 10%. (Book p902)]

In the opening classification of hyperthyroxinemia (elevated T3 and T4 levels), what biochemical finding defines thyrotoxicosis rather than euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia? [Hyperthyroxinemia branches into thyrotoxicosis (defined by elevated free T3/free T4) and euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia (elevated total T3/total T4). (Bo]

Under thyrotoxicosis with elevated free hormone levels, match the gland status to its underlying mechanism — 1) Overworking gland 2) Normal gland … A) Hyperthyroidism B) Stored hormones released / Hormone supplement [In thyrotoxicosis, an overworking gland corresponds to true hyperthyroidism, whereas a normal gland releases stored hormones (thyroiditis) or receives]

Assess these causes of euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia (elevated total T3 and total T4): I TBG excess. II Drugs that inhibit deiodinase-2 (D1-2), Sick euthyroid syndrome, and RTH. [Causes of euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia listed on page 902 include: 1) TBG excess, 2) Drugs that inhibit deiodinase-2, 3) Sick euthyroid syndrome, and 4]

Which of the following is NOT listed on page 902 as a cause of TBG excess? [Causes of TBG excess on page 902 are OCPs, estrogen, pregnancy, steroids, chronic active hepatitis, and inherited TBG excess (rare). Nephrotic syndrom]

A 24-year-old woman taking oral contraceptive pills has high total T4 and total T3 on routine screening. Free T4, free T3, and TSH are normal. What is the diagnosis? [OCPs raise TBG levels, leading to elevated total T3/T4 with normal free hormone levels, classified as euthyroid hyperthyroxinemia. (Book p902)]

What is the primary pathogenesis of Resistance to Thyroid Hormone (RTH)? [In RTH, partial or completely resistant T3/T4 receptors cause uninhibited increase of TSH, producing high T3 and T4 that fail to exert downstream acti]

Match the clinical presentation of Resistance to Thyroid Hormone (RTH) to its relative frequency — 1) Euthyroid state 2) Toxicosis … A) Most common (m/c) B) Rare (due to resistance to TR-β forms) [Clinically in RTH, patients are most commonly euthyroid; toxicosis is rare and occurs due to resistance to beta forms (TR-β). (Book p902)]

In Resistance to Thyroid Hormone (RTH), the rare occurrence of toxicosis is due to resistance specifically involving ___ forms of the receptor. [Toxicosis in RTH is rare and develops due to selective resistance to beta forms (TR-β). (Book p902)]

A male infant presents with severe cognitive impairment and hypotonia. Molecular genetic testing identifies a loss-of-function defect in the neuronal MCT8 transporter. What is the diagnosis? [MCT8 defect causes impaired entry of T3 into neurons, producing Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome characterized by severe cognitive impairment. (Book p902]

In the CNS thyroid hormone transport pathway: I T4 crosses the blood-brain barrier via OATP1C1 and MCT8 into astrocytes, where D2 converts it to T3. II T3 enters neurons via MCT8 to activate T3-responsive genes. [T4 crosses the blood-brain barrier via OATP1C1/MCT8 into astrocytes where deiodinase-2 (D2) converts T4 to T3; T3 then enters neurons via MCT8 to regu]

Which transporter protein is shown alongside MCT8 at the blood-brain barrier for thyroid hormone transport into astrocytes on page 902? [The blood-brain barrier diagram depicts OATP1C1 and MCT8 facilitating thyroid hormone transport into astrocytes. (Book p902)]

elements.source: A patient with a midline neck swelling undergoes Technetium-99m (Tc^99m) scintigraphy. The scan demonstrates no uptake in the normal anatomical location and prominent uptake in an abnormal subhyoid region. What is the diagnosis? [The scintigraphy image on page 903 shows a Tc-99m scan of ectopic thyroid, with 'No uptake in normal location' and 'Uptake in ectopic location'. (Book]

Match the thyroid disorder to its effect on the Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) — 1) Hypothyroidism 2) Hyperthyroidism … A) Decreased (↓) BMR B) Increased (↑) BMR [Thyroid hormone maintains BMR: hypothyroidism leads to decreased BMR, whereas hyperthyroidism causes increased BMR. (Book p903)]

Which receptor family is explicitly listed under 'Cardiac actions' of thyroid hormone on page 903? [Page 903 explicitly notes: 'Cardiac actions (α-receptors): ↑ Cardiac output (CO), ↑ O2 utilization, ↑ heart rate'. (Book p903)]

Thyroid hormone stimulates tissue oxygen (O2) utilization throughout the body, with the explicit exception of the ___ and ___. [Thyroid hormone causes increased O2 utilization '(Except brain & gonads)'. (Book p903)]

Regarding the vascular and hemodynamic effects on page 903: I Toxicosis leads directly to increased cardiac output (CO). II Hyperthyroidism increases peripheral resistance, leading to increased blood pressure (BP). [Page 903 notes: 'Toxicosis -> ↑ CO' and 'Hyperthyroidism -> ↑ peripheral resistance -> ↑ BP'. (Book p903)]

Thyroid hormone drives thermogenesis by acting as an uncoupler of ___; a severe deficiency in myxedema coma causes ___. [Thyroid hormone acts as an uncoupler of oxidative phosphorylation producing thermogenesis; its lack in myxedema coma results in hypothermia. (Book p90]

What two key effects of thyroid hormone on carbohydrate metabolism are outlined on page 903? [In carbohydrate metabolism, thyroid hormone drives: 1. Gluconeogenesis, and 2. Glucose uptake into cells (with hypothyroidism predisposing to insulin ]

Regarding fat metabolism: I Thyroid hormone causes minimal lipolysis. II Thyroid hormone stimulates cholesterol clearance; therefore, hypothyroidism results in hypercholesterolemia. [Under fat metabolism: 1. Lipolysis (minimal), 2. Cholesterol clearance (Hypothyroidism : Hypercholesterolemia). (Book p903)]

A patient with severe long-standing thyrotoxicosis develops proximal muscle wasting, osteopenia with pathological fractures, and hypercalcemia with nephrolithiasis. What catabolic mechanism explains these findings? [In significant toxicosis, thyroid hormone acts as a potent catabolic hormone driving proteolysis -> myopathy, osteopenia -> osteoporosis, and hypercal]

Match the physiological action of thyroid hormone to its target organ — 1) CNS 2) Vitamin metabolism 3) Bone marrow … A) Myelination B) β-Carotene conversion to Vitamin A C) Stimulates erythropoiesis [Thyroid hormone promotes myelination of the CNS, converts beta-carotene to vitamin A, and stimulates erythropoiesis in bone marrow. (Book p903)]

Why can hypothyroid patients exhibit yellowish-orange skin discoloration while sparing the sclerae? [Thyroid hormone is responsible for converting beta-carotene to vitamin A; in hypothyroidism this conversion is impaired, leading to hypercarotenemia a]

Thyroid hormone maintains reproductive fertility; the sequential menstrual derangement noted in untreated hypothyroidism is: menorrhagia → ___ → infertility. [Under fertility maintenance: 'Hypothyroidism -> menorrhagia -> Oligo/amenorrhea -> Infertility'. (Book p903)]

Which of the following is NOT listed on page 903 as a physiologic function or target of thyroid hormone? [Thyroid hormone stimulates erythropoiesis, not inhibits it. It also maintains BMR, promotes CNS myelination, and converts beta-carotene to vitamin A. ]

elements.source: Match the drug categories affecting thyroid function tests — 1) Deiodinase inhibitors 2) Enzyme inducers (↑ hormone metabolism) … A) Steroids, Propranolol, Iodine, Amiodarone, Propylthiouracil B) Phenytoin, Carbamazepine, Rifampicin, Sertraline, Ritonavir [Deiodinase inhibitors listed are steroids, propranolol, iodine, amiodarone, PTU; enzyme inducers increasing metabolism are phenytoin, carbamazepine, r]

Which of the following drugs is NOT listed on page 904 as a deiodinase inhibitor? [Rifampicin is an enzyme inducer that increases hormone metabolism; steroids, propranolol, iodine, amiodarone, and PTU are deiodinase inhibitors. (Book]

Match the drug to its specific effect on thyroid hormone economy — 1) Lithium 2) Al(OH)3, Cholestyramine, Calcium carbonate, Ferrous sulfate … A) Directly causes hypothyroidism B) Decreases thyroid hormone absorption [Lithium causes hypothyroidism, while aluminum hydroxide, cholestyramine, calcium carbonate, and ferrous sulfate decrease thyroid hormone absorption. (]

What is the normal reference range for TSH tested by 4th-generation CLIA as specified on page 904? [Page 904 states: 'TSH (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone) : 0.5 - 5 mIU/L (by CLIA 4th generation)'. (Book p904)]

Regarding thyroid testing rules on page 904: I Clinicians should always look for all three: fT3, fT4, and TSH. II Thyroid function tests should not be checked in critically ill patients. [Under TESTS: 'Always look for all of: fT3, fT4, TSH' and 'Do not check in critically ill patients'. (Book p904)]

A patient's laboratory report reveals: TSH elevated (↑), while total T4, free T4, total T3, and free T3 are all normal (N). What is the condition? [TSH ↑ with normal T4, FT4, T3, and FT3 represents Subclinical 1° hypothyroidism. (Book p904)]

In overt primary hypothyroidism (TSH ↑, T4 ↓, FT4 ↓, T3 ↓, FT3 ↓), what is the most common etiology and clinical association noted on page 904? [For primary hypothyroidism, page 904 notes: 'm/c : Autoimmune' and 'A/w : Hashimoto's thyroiditis'. (Book p904)]

A patient's thyroid panel shows elevation of all parameters: TSH ↑, T4 ↑, FT4 ↑, T3 ↑, and FT3 ↑. Clinically, the patient is euthyroid. What is the diagnosis? [When TSH, T4, FT4, T3, and FT3 are all elevated, the condition is RTH if the patient is euthyroid, or TSH-secreting adenoma if toxic features are pres]

When TSH, T4, FT4, T3, and FT3 are all simultaneously elevated, match the clinical presentation to the diagnosis — 1) Euthyroid state 2) Toxic features present … A) RTH (Resistance to Thyroid Hormone) B) TSH secreting adenoma [For elevated TSH + elevated T4/FT4/T3/FT3: RTH presents as euthyroid; TSH secreting adenoma presents with toxic features. (Book p904)]

In hypothalamo-pituitary (secondary) hypothyroidism: I TSH is normal or decreased (N/↓). II T4, FT4, T3, and FT3 are all decreased (↓). [In hypothalamo-pituitary hypothyroidism, TSH is normal or low (N/↓) while peripheral hormones T4, FT4, T3, and FT3 are all low (↓). (Book p904)]

A patient has TSH ↓, total T4 normal, free T4 ↑, total T3 normal, and free T3 ↑. Which causes does the page 904 interpretation table list for this pattern? [Under thyrotoxicosis (TSH ↓, T4 N, FT4 ↑, T3 N, FT3 ↑), causes include overworking gland (Autoimmune Graves) and stored hormone release (Thyroiditis, ]

Serum thyroglobulin is elevated in all forms of thyrotoxicosis EXCEPT ___, where exogenous hormone suppresses endogenous thyroglobulin release. [Serum thyroglobulin is increased in all thyrotoxicosis except thyrotoxicosis factitia (hormone supplementation). (Book p904)]
